upstream.scope: Action acknowledgement kept apart from the observed process outcome (D1 §§18.2, Appendix B, 27; D2 T24; S1 htop 3.5.3 kill workflow for comparison only): the actions status says what the server did with a request, and a separate observed-outcome line (node 88) says what srtop's own scans saw of the exact process instance afterwards, watched for 10 s on the gate's suspend-aware clock: exited after the request, still running, or outcome unknown, never escalated. Settlement reuses the runtime's event result cache: every handler result is committed state settled PROCESSED, a redelivery after a broken transport is DUPLICATE at the original revision_after_effect, REJECTED is event validation only. Intents and the watch live only in the srtop process. No protocol message, registry entry, SDK, runtime, renderer or client change; no new dependency. Closes HTOP-R1-001's last owner ticket

entries.feature: The request and the observed outcome are published apart: ACTIONS_STATUS (node 87) keeps the request's result ('Requested #n (…): SIGTERM was sent; the process may handle or ignore it, and what is observed of it afterwards is reported separately'), and ACTIONS_OBSERVED (node 88, a Text with the Status role, bounded to MAX_OBSERVED_BYTES 512) says 'Observed outcome: no sent request is being watched', 'Watching #n', 'Exited after the request #n', 'Still running #n' or 'Outcome unknown #n'; only a signal the kernel accepted (Execution::Requested with --actions terminate) is watched, never a dry run, refusal, failure or unsupported result; both fit ACTIONS_RESERVE_BYTES at their widest

entries.feature: A sent request is watched by its exact ProcessKey until a deadline (DEFAULT_OBSERVATION_WINDOW 10 s on the gate's suspend-aware clock); at the deadline the latest scan sampled after the request settles it as still running (listed) or outcome unknown (no such scan, the view paused or resuming, or the scan neither lists it nor establishes an exit); nothing is ever sent again: no second SIGTERM, no SIGKILL, no retry; the deadline is enforced by every sample and by the refresh loop's own timer, so it settles on time while paused and with no tick; one request is watched at a time and a newer sent request replaces the watch; the loop's deadline timer re-checks at least every second (OBSERVATION_RECHECK), so a deadline passed during a host sleep settles within about a second of waking

entries.feature: Attribution: 'exited after the request' only when a scan sampled after the settlement (the second the view applies after it, ActionTargets::scans) establishes before the deadline that the exact instance is gone (another instance confirmed under its PID, or its last-observed record's verdict is an exit; the watched key is kept in the view's watched set so that record exists); never an unconfirmed, unreadable, capped or evicted row, never another process, and the line never says srtop ended it ('whether SIGTERM or something else ended it is not known'); an exit before the settlement is never attributed (a scan that saw it withdraws the intent; an exit after the last scan makes the handle unobtainable, so the request is refused, nothing sent, nothing watched); a zombie, which accepts the signal and stays listed, is reported still running with the caveat, never exited; a target already exited but unreaped when Confirm arrives accepts the signal and is later reported exited after the request (no cause claimed)

entries.feature: Settlement through the existing event result cache, no second acknowledgement protocol: every handler result (refused at Prepare, requested, refused by the terminator, unsupported) is committed state and settles PROCESSED; its redelivery is DUPLICATE, accepted, at the same revision_after_effect, committing and sending nothing; REJECTED only from event validation (disabled or absent node, future observed_revision); a transport broken after the effect and before the acknowledgement, then CLIENT_RESUME (RESUME_OK with a frontier covering the event) and a replay of the pending event, is answered from the cache: the client shows the settled result and an owned worker has received exactly one SIGTERM

A daemon restart abandons every intent and watch: they live only in the srtop process and nothing is persisted; the new instance answers RESYNC_REQUIRED{REPLACED}, its snapshot has no confirmation panel, Cancel disabled and the observed line idle; an old Confirm replayed anyway names no node and is rejected; an owned worker receives nothing more; every run draws its own panel node range (2^32 + k·12288, k uniform among 2^39), so an old Confirm names no node of the new run even once the new run shows a panel in the same slot and has passed the old click's revision (verification round 1, F1; residual collision 2^-39 per pair of runs)

entries.feature: Intent and settlement are logged without sensitive arguments: ActionLog (production StderrActionLog, the only eprintln! that is not 'srtop: …: {error}', pinned by command_line_test) receives one line per prepared, refused, requested, failed, unsupported, cancelled, withdrawn, watched and observed event, of fixed words, the intent number, operation, PID and UID, bounded to MAX_ACTION_LOG_BYTES 160; no process name, command line, environment, path or reason text
